doc.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: The Kansas City sound and Bennie Moten
summary: He says Kansas City stamped musicians' style and recalls Bennie Moten's two-four beat success in New York.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Coming up being born in Oklahoma, which was the southwest at that time, can you describe for us how the southwest sound, like the Count Basie sound, was different from the sounds on the east coast or the west coast?

Oh yeah, well it was different but I mean I don’t know how I can explain to you the difference because in fact the Kansas City was different from any of the styles. Boys would come up from the south and Texas and Louisiana and all through there but they’d come through Kansas City and they changed their style somewhere. Because anytime you would tell somebody you’re from Kansas City, they know that you are a good musician. If you’ve got the Kansas City stamp you’ve got it made. I can’t tell you. It’s different but I can’t put my finger on it. I know at one time Bennie Moten left Kansas City and came to New York. And he made it real big with what they call a two four beat, instead of playing a number like [scats]. He played [scats]. And they fell in love with Bennie Moten’s band.
